precepts.text: Take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and their seed shall inherit the land.
precepts.point: Every tribe keeps to the inheritance of its fathers.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
Numbers 36 is the law for the brother who had no sons. The chief fathers of Gilead, of the tribe of Manasseh, came before Moses because the inheritance of Zelophehad was given to his daughters, and “if they be married to any of the sons of the other tribes of the children of Israel, then shall their inheritance be taken from the inheritance of our fathers”. The inheritance goes to her husband. Not even the jubile would bring it back: “so shall their inheritance be taken away from the inheritance of the tribe of our fathers.” You are Manasseh, you marry into Judah, and Judah owns that land forever.

So the Lord commanded, “only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry”, “that the children of Israel may enjoy every man the inheritance of his fathers.” That is the law right there: if you have all daughters and you have land and property, they marry within the tribe so another tribe of Israel does not take possession of it forever.

That is what Tobit was making reference to. Brothers often ask, because Judah married outside the tribe of Judah and Ephraim married outside the tribe of Ephraim. But there was a special clause when it came to property and land, and the woman was not allowed to do that.

Tobit tells his son, “chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe”. See that: not of thy father’s tribe. “for we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob”, and “our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.” Shall inherit the land: that is the point. Marrying your own kindred is how the inheritance of the fathers stays with their seed.

precepts.text: In pride is destruction, and lewdness is the mother of famine.
precepts.point: Every tribe keeps to the inheritance of its fathers.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
Tobit keeps going, and it is for anybody here looking at a Chinese lady: “love thy brethren, and despise not in thy heart thy brethren, the sons and daughters of thy people, in not taking a wife of them: for in pride is destruction and much trouble”. It is pride when you do not want to marry a woman of your own race, your own tribe. When people say love is love, that has nothing to do with it; God never said hate your people.

“and in lewdness is decay and great want: for lewdness is the mother of famine.” You will lose everything, and you see it all in the news. Halle Berry married outside and now pays child support to both of her exes, thousands every month, while the white husband she paid called her a nigger every time she paid. He fought to straighten and lighten their daughter’s natural hair, because he wanted his children to look white. She knew what she was up against.

Serena and Venus Williams married outside the race after all the hell their father went through for those two girls. He saw the power of white supremacy get into his daughter’s head, and he did not show up at the wedding. Janet Jackson married an Arab and ran out of there with the baby, under an agreement not to speak on what she saw. Shannon Sharpe lost millions and millions of dollars over a twenty-year-old white girl from the gym.

That is lewdness being the mother of famine, decay and great want. The Bible is a true book. The law of Numbers 36 kept the inheritance in the tribe of the fathers, and Tobit shows the curse on those who despise their own people and take a strange woman.

precepts.text: Let them marry to whom they think best, only within the tribe of their father, so the inheritance does not remove from tribe to tribe.
precepts.point: But what if a daughter who received the inheritance married into another tribe? You have to go precept upon precept: Numbers 36 takes up that very case with these same daughters. The chief fathers of Gilead brought it to Moses, and the word came back that the daughters of Zelophehad may marry to whom they think best, only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry.

note.label: Numbers 27: The Daughters of Zelophehad and the Ordination of Joshua

precepts.why:
The Lord set the order of inheritance for all Israel: to the daughter if there is no son, then to the brethren, then to the father's brethren, then to the next kinsman of his family. Every angle was covered so the inheritance stayed within the tribe. Israel always had questions, just as we do when we read, and the Lord put these statutes in place to answer them before they were asked.

But what if a daughter who received the inheritance married into another tribe? You have to go precept upon precept: Numbers 36 takes up that very case with these same daughters. The chief fathers of Gilead brought it to Moses, and the word came back: “This is the thing which the Lord doth command concerning the daughters of Zelophehad, saying, Let them marry to whom they think best; only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry.”

“So shall not the inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe: for every one of the children of Israel shall keep himself to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers.” Where an inheritance rode on the marriage, the woman married within her father's tribe.

precepts.text: Every daughter that possesses an inheritance shall be wife unto one of the family of the tribe of her father, that every man enjoy the inheritance of his fathers.
precepts.point: But what if a daughter who received the inheritance married into another tribe? You have to go precept upon precept: Numbers 36 takes up that very case with these same daughters. The chief fathers of Gilead brought it to Moses, and the word came back that the daughters of Zelophehad may marry to whom they think best, only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry.

note.label: Numbers 27: The Daughters of Zelophehad and the Ordination of Joshua

precepts.why:
The statute of judgment in Numbers 27 passed the inheritance to the daughter, and Numbers 36 settles whom that daughter marries. “And every daughter, that possesseth an inheritance in any tribe of the children of Israel, shall be wife unto one of the family of the tribe of her father, that the children of Israel may enjoy every man the inheritance of his fathers.”

“Neither shall the inheritance remove from one tribe to another tribe; but every one of the tribes of the children of Israel shall keep himself to his own inheritance.” This is not saying no one ever married from Judah to Benjamin or Levi to Ephraim; it is showing that where an inheritance rode on the marriage, the woman married within her father's tribe, that every man enjoy the inheritance of his fathers.

precepts.text: The daughters of Zelophehad were married unto their father's brothers' sons, and the inheritance remained in the tribe of the family of their father.
precepts.point: But what if a daughter who received the inheritance married into another tribe? You have to go precept upon precept: Numbers 36 takes up that very case with these same daughters. The chief fathers of Gilead brought it to Moses, and the word came back that the daughters of Zelophehad may marry to whom they think best, only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry.

note.label: Numbers 27: The Daughters of Zelophehad and the Ordination of Joshua

precepts.why:
The daughters whose case brought this statute of judgment did as it was commanded. “Even as the Lord commanded Moses, so did the daughters of Zelophehad: For Mahlah, Tirzah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, were married unto their father’s brothers’ sons.”

“And they were married into the families of the sons of Manasseh the son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained in the tribe of the family of their father.” The inheritance that passed to them under Numbers 27 stayed in Manasseh, because they married their father's brothers' sons.

precepts.text: The daughters of Zelophehad pleaded that their father died in his own sin with no son, and asked why his name should be done away from among his family.
precepts.point: Their concern is real: if the daughters marry men of another tribe, their father's inheritance passes with them to the husband's tribe, and at the jubilee it is fixed to that tribe, so the tribe of Manasseh loses that land forever.

note.label: Numbers 36: The Inheritance of the Daughters of Zelophehad

precepts.why:
The chief fathers of Gilead, of the tribe of Manasseh, bring an issue rising out of what was already ruled in Numbers 27. Zelophehad died in the wilderness with no sons, and his daughters had pleaded: “Our father died in the wilderness, and he was not in the company of them that gathered themselves together against the Lord in the company of Korah; but died in his own sin, and had no sons.”

“Why should the name of our father be done away from among his family, because he hath no son? Give unto us therefore a possession among the brethren of our father.” That plea is where the inheritance of Zelophehad’s daughters came from, and it is the inheritance the fathers of Gilead now fear to lose to another tribe.

precepts.text: The Lord ruled the daughters spoke right: if a man die and have no son, his inheritance passes to his daughter; that ruling set up the question of Numbers 36.
precepts.point: Their concern is real: if the daughters marry men of another tribe, their father's inheritance passes with them to the husband's tribe, and at the jubilee it is fixed to that tribe, so the tribe of Manasseh loses that land forever.

note.label: Numbers 36: The Inheritance of the Daughters of Zelophehad

precepts.why:
“And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying, The daughters of Zelophehad speak right: thou shalt surely give them a possession of an inheritance among their father’s brethren; and thou shalt cause the inheritance of their father to pass unto them.” The Lord ruled that Zelophehad’s inheritance pass to his daughters, and made it law: “If a man die, and have no son, then ye shall cause his inheritance to pass unto his daughter.”

That ruling set up the question of Numbers 36. The concern of the chief fathers is real: if the daughters marry men of another tribe, their father’s inheritance passes with them to the husband’s tribe, and at the jubile it is fixed to that tribe, so the tribe of Manasseh loses that land forever.

precepts.text: Take a wife of the seed of thy fathers and not a strange woman; the seed-of-thy-fathers command still stands, and the tribe clause belonged to the inheritance law of Numbers 36.
precepts.point: No one today knows his exact tribe with certainty; a Judahite could have been dropped off anywhere in the captivity. Without the history of Numbers 36, Tobit 4:12 gets twisted into a doctrine that a man may only marry his own tribe, and that is a heresy born of not knowing why the law was given.

note.label: Numbers 36: The Inheritance of the Daughters of Zelophehad

precepts.why:
Every daughter that possessed an inheritance had to marry within her father’s tribe, “that the children of Israel may enjoy every man the inheritance of his fathers”, and no inheritance would remove from one tribe to another. That restriction belonged to the time when Israel dwelt in the land; it existed because of inheritance.

Tobit told his son: “Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe: for we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.”

The seed-of-thy-fathers command still stands: take a wife of the seed of thy fathers and not a strange woman. The tribe clause belonged to the inheritance law of Numbers 36. Today Israel has no inheritance in the lands of captivity, so the rule that still applies is marrying within the nation of Israel, not tribe-only marriage. No one today knows his exact tribe with certainty; a Judahite could have been dropped off anywhere in the captivity. Without the history of Numbers 36, Tobit 4:12 gets twisted into a doctrine that a man may only marry his own tribe, and that is a heresy born of not knowing why the law was given.

precepts.text: The chief fathers of Gilead brought the case of the daughters of Zelophehad: if the daughters married into another tribe, their inheritance would be taken from the inheritance of the fathers and put to the tribe wherein they were received, and fixed there at the jubile.
precepts.point: What is this going back to? The law of the land, the law of inheritance when it comes to land, read back in the book of Numbers. The husband died and the two sons died, and the only person left is the wife with the land; so she instinctively went to Boaz, and Boaz is now conducting the laws of the land of who it should be passed down to, going down the list of inheritance.
precepts.why:
Boaz is conducting the laws of the land, going down the list of who the inheritance should be passed to, and that goes back to the law of land inheritance in Numbers. “And the chief fathers of the families of the children of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, of the families of the sons of Joseph, came near, and spake before Moses, and before the princes, the chief fathers of the children of Israel”.

They brought the case of the daughters of Zelophehad: “The Lord commanded my lord to give the land for an inheritance by lot to the children of Israel: and my lord was commanded by the Lord to give the inheritance of Zelophehad our brother unto his daughters. And if they be married to any of the sons of the other tribes of the children of Israel, then shall their inheritance be taken from the inheritance of our fathers, and shall be put to the inheritance of the tribe whereunto they are received”. And at the jubile it would be fixed there, taken away from the inheritance of the tribe of their fathers.

Reading between the lines, you were able to marry outside your particular tribe. You can be Judah and marry somebody from Manasseh, or Manasseh and marry somebody from Ephraim; that is why they had this complaint in the first place. It just has to be within the twelve tribes of Israel, inside your nation, not outside with the heathen. Elimelech's husband and sons died and only Naomi was left with the land, so she instinctively went to Boaz, and he is now applying this law.

precepts.text: The answer: let them marry to whom they think best, only to the family of the tribe of their father, so that no inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe.
precepts.point: What is this going back to? The law of the land, the law of inheritance when it comes to land, read back in the book of Numbers. The husband died and the two sons died, and the only person left is the wife with the land; so she instinctively went to Boaz, and Boaz is now conducting the laws of the land of who it should be passed down to, going down the list of inheritance.
precepts.why:
The answer given through Moses: “The tribe of the sons of Joseph hath said well. This is the thing which the Lord doth command concerning the daughters of Zelophehad, saying, Let them marry to whom they think best; only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry.”

“So shall not the inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe: for every one of the children of Israel shall keep himself to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers.” Every daughter that possessed an inheritance was to be wife to one of the family of the tribe of her father, “that the children of Israel may enjoy every man the inheritance of his fathers.”

That is the law of the land Boaz is going by. The land which was our brother Elimelech's must stay with the family, so Boaz goes down the list: the nearer kinsman first, and I am after thee. Marrying outside the tribe was fine within the twelve tribes of Israel; the point of the law is that the inheritance does not remove from tribe to tribe, and never goes outside the nation.
